why: Takes one --only value whole instead of splitting it, so `--only a,b,c` becomes the single id "a,b,c". That id matches nothing, so this particular regression stops the run rather than under-running it -- but it still turns a working spelling into a hard refusal. The test pins the comma list as a real multi-id spelling, not a name.
killedBy: parseArgs splits one --only on commas, and mixes commas with repeats
